data.name: Gerrit
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German name Gerhard, meaning 'spear-strong' or 'brave with a spear'. The name Gerrit was popular among the Dutch and German populations and may have been influenced by the Old Norse name Gjörríðr, meaning 'helmswoman' or 'protector'.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who embody strength and courage, and are protectors and leaders in their communities.

in_english.name: Gerald
in_english.meaning: Ruler with the spear, powerful with a lance
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German name Gisilheri, which is composed of the elements gisil (pledge, hostage) and hari (ruler, warrior). The English name Gerald is a variation of this, incorporating the Old English word ger (spear) and the Old High German word ald (ruler, powerful).

biblical_reference.note: The region of Gerasenes is mentioned in the New Testament as the site of the healing of the Gerasene demon-possessed man by Jesus.
